rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 (kp 4.0, kd 0.25, ki 0.3, base_speed 1.3) is the best raced design so far at 74.19. Every trial on all three tracks still went off track, with one line-loss event per run. max_error sits at 0.062 to 0.065 m on every track whatever the gains (iterations 0 to 4), so gain changes have not moved that floor. The oval steering_oscillation is 0.254, above the 0.2 concern level, but the other tracks are at 0.12 to 0.13. Raising ki (iteration 2) lowered progress, and raising kp (iteration 3) did not reduce max_error.

Change: move both sensor rows from y = 0.04 to y = 0.06 m, keeping x, weights, and all controller values unchanged (kp 4.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.3, last_direction). This is the geometry test the feedback asked for. Moving the sensors forward gives earlier look-ahead, so the controller sees the bend before the wheels reach it, which is a plausible cause of the fixed off-track floor.

Expected result: max_error falls below about 0.058 m and line_loss_events drop on some seeds. Steering_oscillation may rise slightly because the signal reacts earlier, so I will watch it. Risk: the longer look-ahead can overshoot on tight bends.

Hypotheses: (1) the max_error floor is caused by look-ahead distance, not gain; (2) kd 0.25 is enough damping to keep oscillation near 0.2 with earlier sensing. Measurements wanted: max_error, line_loss_events, progress, steering_oscillation, rms_error, and control_effort on every track. Next step depends on the result. If max_error falls and oscillation stays under about 0.2, try base_speed toward 1.8 once progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. If the score falls below 74.19 or oscillation exceeds about 0.25, revert to y = 0.04 and try kp 5 with kd 0.3.
